en: The Jātaka:
The Ninth Chapter, The Section on Vultures (Gijjhavagga)
9. The Haliddirāga Jātaka:
“In the forest, at a secluded lodging, one who is patient with praise—”
“And those who endure [the hardships] in the village are even more exalted than you.
“Having come from the forest to the village,”
“Of what character and what conduct should I serve as a man, O father?
Tell me that when I ask you.”
“O dear one, he who would inspire confidence in you,
and who would forgive your lack of confidence;
who is obedient and patient— ”
Go from here and associate with him,
in whom there is no evil done by body, speech, or mind.
Having established yourself as if upon your own breast,
follow him once you have departed from here—
he who conducts himself according to the Dhamma.
Even while practicing, he does not conceive conceits;
go from here and associate with that wise one who acts with purity.
O dear one, do not associate with such a person— one who is dyed like turmeric, whose mind is like a monkey, and who is both lustful and free from lust.
Even if one were to become a god,
one would still be like an angry venomous snake,
or like a great highway smeared with filth.
Avoid them from afar,
just as one avoids a dangerous path;
for, dear son, misfortunes increase.
For one who excessively associates with a fool,
do not ever associate with that fool,
as if with an enemy.
Therefore, my dear, I entreat you:
do as I say;
do not associate with fools.
“Suffering is association with fools.
Thus ends the ninth Jātaka, the Haliddirāga Jātaka.
